title: Anthology quiz, poems 1 to 8
subject: English Literature
unit: Spring 2: Anthology poetry: poems 1 to 8 and comparison (Component 1 Section B)
source: Seeded from english-literature/y10 lesson 49 (Anthology quiz, poems 1 to 8 (portal))
intro: Covers lessons 9 to 49 of Anthology poetry: poems 1 to 8 and comparison (Component 1 Section B). Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: What does the child fear most?
questions.a: C) Being made less than human. The poem's deepest fear is dehumanisation, shown in images of machines and stone.

questions.q: Why is the first stanza only two lines?
options: Its shortness mirrors the lack of water
questions.a: A) Its shortness mirrors the lack of water. Form mirrors content: scarcity of lines matches scarcity of water.

questions.q: Why does Bhatt put Gujarati in the middle of the poem?
options: To show her mother tongue at the heart of her identity
questions.a: B) To show her mother tongue at the heart of her identity. Its central place and returning power show it is at the core of who she is.

questions.q: What does 'I weep like a child for the past' show?
options: The adult is overwhelmed by nostalgia
questions.a: C) The adult is overwhelmed by nostalgia. The simile shows memory turning a man back into a child.

questions.q: Why does Shakespeare use a seamark and a star?
options: Both are fixed guides that stay steady in storms
questions.a: A) Both are fixed guides that stay steady in storms. Lighthouses and the Pole Star guide sailors and never move: images of constancy.

questions.q: Which sentence compares methods?
options: Lawrence uses rhyming couplets to suggest a song, whereas Scannell's single stanza traps the reader with the child.
questions.a: A) Lawrence uses rhyming couplets to suggest a song, whereas Scannell's single stanza traps the reader with the child.. It names a method in each poem and links them; the others only state ideas.

questions.q: Which partner for Prayer Before Birth gives the best comparison?
options: Any poem, it does not matter
If-: both give a voice to the young and a vision of what makes us human
questions.a: B) If-: both give a voice to the young and a vision of what makes us human. If- shares a clear concept (how a person should be shaped) with a strong contrast in voice.

questions.q: Why does Kipling delay the main clause until the end?
options: To make the reward feel earned after every condition
questions.a: C) To make the reward feel earned after every condition. The long run of conditions builds to the promise; the reader must hold every 'if' to reach it.

questions.q: What does the final question suggest?
options: The child has been forgotten and is alone
The child won the game happily
questions.a: B) The child has been forgotten and is alone. The rhetorical question turns victory into isolation.

questions.q: Which DIRT edit gains the most AO3 marks?
options: Adding the second poem's method to every paragraph
questions.a: A) Adding the second poem's method to every paragraph. Integrated comparison of methods is what AO3 rewards.

questions.q: If- is addressed to...
questions.a: B) 'my son'

questions.q: Anaphora means...
questions.a: A) repeating words at the start of lines
options: repeating words at the start of lines

questions.q: Kipling calls Triumph and Disaster...
questions.a: B) impostors

questions.q: Prayer Before Birth was written in...
Prayer Before Birth's refrain is...
questions.a: A) 'I am not yet born'

questions.q: A plea is...
questions.a: B) an urgent request

questions.q: Free verse has...
questions.a: A) no regular rhyme or metre

questions.q: Blessing is set in...
questions.a: B) Mumbai

questions.q: Blessing begins with...
questions.a: B) drought

questions.q: 'silver crashes to the ground' presents water as...
questions.a: A) treasure
